description: Candidate stateful conformance cases for the StoreAdapter surface. The published vectors at ac4468f grade the wire schema, the feed authenticator, the receipt signer and the semantic aggregator; measured under sys.settrace, 1 of 28 executable cases reaches a store adapter at all. These cases exercise adapter BEHAVIOUR instead, and each one names the flattering implementation it exists to catch.
status: CANDIDATE. Proposed, not accepted. Being proposed or merged does not make these G2 or G4 evidence.

authored_by.author: Rastislav Drahos
authored_by.disclosure: inspeximus is itself a G4 adapter candidate, so these cases are authored by an interested party. A separate producer must validate both implementations AND this fixture. Nothing here is independent evidence about inspeximus.
authored_by.coupling: Cases describe store state and expected receipt outcomes abstractly. No case names an inspeximus API. Binding an implementation is one function, `build_adapter(records)`, described in the runner.

how_a_case_is_stated.normative: Where the expected outcome is written down in the specification. Expectations are quoted from the contract, never inferred from the case name. The runner refuses to score a case whose `normative` block is missing, because a case whose expectation nobody wrote down is a case that scores an opinion.
how_a_case_is_stated.positive_control: The adapter methods this case must actually reach. Verified by tracing the run. A case that never reaches the surface it claims to test passes for the wrong reason, which is the defect these cases exist to find.
how_a_case_is_stated.mutation: The flattering implementation this case must catch. The runner applies it and REQUIRES the case to fail. A fixture that has never been shown to fail is a fixture nobody has tested.

adapter_cases.why: A store holding a derived artifact whose inputs were never declared cannot know what that artifact descends from, so it cannot know whether the retired proposition survives inside it. Reporting `verified` there is the difference between an honest receipt and a comfortable one.

normative.quote: No silent completeness: missing lineage, inaccessible stores, backups, provider logs, model weights, screenshots, and copied prose with severed lineage remain `partial` or `unknown`.

records.text: is vegetarian; prefers quiet restaurants; moderate budget
digest whose summariser dropped its lineage

adapter_cases.note: The contract permits `partial` OR `unknown` here, so both are accepted. Pinning the single value our own implementation emits would have failed a conforming adapter that chose the other, and the reference's own test expects `partial` for a related shape.

positive_control.note: Only methods measured to be load-bearing for THIS case are declared. The runner stubs each one in both directions and requires the case to notice; listing a method the case does not actually depend on makes the control a decoration.

mutation.why: This is a real shipped defect, not a hypothetical: inspeximus 2.8.0 answered `verified` for exactly this store and had to be fixed. An adapter cannot be trusted to report incompleteness it has no incentive to report.

adapter_cases.why: The discrimination twin of the case above, and the reason that one means anything. An adapter hard-wired to answer `unknown` passes every honesty case ever written while being useless. Without this case the suite rewards permanent pessimism exactly as much as honesty.

normative.quote: Aggregate success requires every required store to be `verified`.

mutation.why: Catches the constant-pessimist adapter that would otherwise score full marks on every honesty case in this file.

adapter_cases.why: The published confidentiality case asks only whether a forbidden value is absent from the receipt. An importer whose repair returns an empty receipt satisfies that perfectly. Absence has to be absence FROM a receipt that did the work.

normative.quote: Erasure fixtures carry only fixed content-free protocol labels, timestamps, verdicts, and digests. They never contain a retired value or raw provider response.

positive_control.note: Only methods measured to be load-bearing for THIS case are declared. The runner stubs each one in both directions and requires the case to notice; listing a method the case does not actually depend on makes the control a decoration.

mutation.flattering_behaviour: conceal instead of erase: keep the value verbatim in a side field and demote the record out of present-tense recall
mutation.why: Measured: an adapter doing exactly this scored a full PASS on the earlier version of this case while the store still held the erased value verbatim.

adapter_cases.why: A repair that satisfies the negative postcondition by deleting everything reachable is the cheapest possible cheat and passes any check that only asks whether the retired proposition is gone.

normative.quote: Probes supply behavioral evidence: the stale belief did not reappear in a declared sample, the replacement activated, and collateral facts survived.

mutation.flattering_behaviour: retire every record in the store rather than the gated ones
mutation.why: Confirms the preservation arm can actually fail. A preservation check that never fails is a demonstration.

adapter_cases.known_result: FAILS for both inspeximus and the reference MarkdownAdapter, and the cause is neither adapter. RebuildStrategy introduces the replacement only through rebuild() of a mixed descendant, so a superseded root with no mixed descendant is retired while the correction is never asserted. Measured four ways in probes/rebuildstrategy_loses_the_replacement_without_a_descendant.py: both implementations fail without a descendant and both succeed with one. The receipt stays honest (aggregate=failed), so this is a repair that cannot succeed for this store shape, not one that claims falsely to have succeeded.

validator_anti_vacuity_cases.why: Not a claim about any adapter: a check on the VALIDATOR. Any pass condition of the form 'the forbidden value is not present' is satisfied perfectly by a receipt containing nothing.
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.harness_mutation: repair() returns an object whose serialised form is empty
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.must_produce: the validator reports FAIL for the confidentiality case
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.measured: Before this fixture existed, our own runner scored 28/28 against exactly this stub.

validator_anti_vacuity_cases.why: A check on the VALIDATOR. When an accept-side case passes on 'no exception was raised', a verify_feed that returns its input unchanged satisfies every accept case in the suite.
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.harness_mutation: verify_feed returns its input unchanged and never raises
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.must_produce: the validator reports FAIL for every accept-side feed case, not only for the reject-side ones
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.measured: Our runner passed key-rotation-valid and the split-view case against this stub until an acceptance was required to return every event.

validator_anti_vacuity_cases.why: A check on the VALIDATOR. Where most cases in a section legitimately expect `unknown`, an aggregator hard-wired to `unknown` scores most of that section without evaluating anything.
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.harness_mutation: the semantic aggregator returns `unknown` regardless of evidence
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.must_produce: the validator reports FAIL, because the section must produce at least three distinct verdicts
validator_anti_vacuity_cases.measured: Five of the eight published semantic cases passed against this stub in our runner.

awaiting_specification.why: A repair that re-asserts inputs it never gated leaves the store asserting the same fact twice. The receipt cannot see it: preservation asks whether a term is recallable, and a duplicated fact is recallable exactly as well as a single one. This is a defect class the triad is structurally blind to, so it needs a case that reads the store.

records.text: is vegetarian; prefers quiet restaurants; moderate budget

mutation.flattering_behaviour: re-assert every named input, including inputs that were never gated and are still active
mutation.why: Our own defect. It survived a passing triad and was visible only by reading the store.

awaiting_specification.not_scored_because: StoreAdapter.rebuild names parameters; the specification does not yet define provider-neutral proposition identity, multiplicity or cardinality. The maintainer asked that a candidate fixture not manufacture that normative rule by quotation, and he is right. Our own citation check reached the same verdict independently and refused to score the case: the source it named was a function signature plus our interpretation, which is not a contract. The underlying blind spot is real -- a duplicated proposition is recallable exactly as well as a single one, so the preservation arm cannot see it -- and it stays here as a specification request rather than a conformance case.

target.note: The runner asserts the bound adapter matches these and digests the tree it scores, so an arbitrary --pkg cannot be reported under this fixture's name.
